nodes.description: Tumor cells lack CYLD protein. CYLD is a deubiquitinase directed at non-K48 (K63-linked) polyubiquitin chains on signalling intermediates, including TRAF2, TRAF6, NEMO, Bcl-3 and Dishevelled, so its loss releases several growth and survival pathways at once. CYLD protein is normally prominent in the inner root sheath of the hair follicle and in eccrine glands, matching the lineages of the tumors.

evidence.reference_title: CYLD is a deubiquitinating enzyme that negatively regulates NF-kappaB activation by TNFR family members.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that CYLD is a deubiquitinating enzyme that negatively regulates activation of the transcription factor NF-kappaB by specific tumour-necrosis factor receptors (TNFRs). Loss of the deubiquitinating activity of CYLD correlates with tumorigenesis.

nodes.description: CYLD-null clones expand into benign adnexal tumors with follicular (trichoepithelioma) or sweat-gland-like (cylindroma, spiradenoma) differentiation, often several histologies in one patient and hybrid spiradenocylindromas in one lesion. Many arise independently, so tumor number rises with age. Benign tumors frequently carry further clonal mutations in the epigenetic modifiers DNMT3A and BCOR (29% of benign tumors in one series), with marked intra-tumor heterogeneity; the contribution of those mutations to growth or transformation is not established.

nodes.description: Full skin examination by a dermatologist at least annually, assessing tumor burden, the rate of new tumors, and signs of malignant transformation (rapid growth, bleeding, ulceration, or a change from the patient's usual tumors). Because the first tumor typically appears around puberty, clarifying the genetic status of at-risk relatives, including children, identifies those who would benefit from early treatment.

nodes.description: CYLD binds and deubiquitinates p53, and is needed for p53 stabilization and activation after DNA damage. Ubiquitin chain-restriction analysis suggests CYLD removes K48 chains from p53 indirectly by cleaving K63 linkages in mixed chains. Loss of CYLD catalytic activity impairs this response in epithelial cells and sensitizes mice to chemical carcinogen-induced skin and intestinal tumors, and CYLD deficiency reduces CEP-1/p53-dependent germ cell apoptosis in C. elegans. This arm rests on model-system and biochemical evidence only; p53 stabilization has not been reported in tumors from CYLD cutaneous syndrome patients in the sources cited here, so its contribution to the human tumors is a hypothesis.

evidence.reference_title: The tumour suppressor CYLD regulates the p53 DNA damage response
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, CYLD interacts with and deubiquitinates p53 facilitating its stabilization in response to genotoxic stress.

evidence.reference_title: The tumour suppressor CYLD regulates the p53 DNA damage response
evidence.snippet: Moreover, CYLD deficiency also diminishes CEP-1/p53-dependent DNA damage-induced germ cell apoptosis in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans.

nodes.description: Inherited CYLD-defective cylindromas do not carry the MYB-NFIB fusion found in sporadic cylindromas but still overexpress MYB and its target genes, and MYB knockdown reduces cylindroma cell proliferation, so the inherited and sporadic tumors converge on MYB activation by different routes.

evidence.snippet: Strikingly, none of the inherited CYLD-defective (n = 23) tumours expressed MYB-NFIB fusion transcripts. However, MYB expression was increased in the majority of tumours (69%)

evidence.reference_title: Overexpression of MYB drives proliferation of CYLD-defective cylindroma cells.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, knock-down of MYB expression caused a significant reduction in cylindroma cell proliferation, suggesting that MYB is also a key player and oncogenic driver in inherited cylindromas.

nodes.description: Multiple benign adnexal tumors on the scalp and face, and frequently on the trunk and in sun-protected genital and axillary skin. The first tumor typically appears around puberty and tumors accumulate through adulthood. In two large families the mean age at onset was 16 years (range 8-30), 23% of surveyed patients had undergone total scalp removal, and tumors were on the scalp in 81%, the trunk in 69% and the pubic area in 42%. GeneReviews states that females often have more tumors than males; the same family study found roughly equal numbers of affected men and women but 5 of the 6 total scalp removals were in women.

nodes.description: CYLD binds NEMO and TRAF2 and removes their activating non-K48 polyubiquitin, so its loss augments TNF-receptor-family (CD40, EDAR, XEDAR) activation of canonical NF-kappaB and increases resistance to apoptosis. In keratinocytes, CYLD also deubiquitinates Bcl-3 and keeps it out of the nucleus; Cyld-null keratinocytes accumulate nuclear Bcl-3 with p50 and p52, raise cyclin D1 and proliferate. EDAR and XEDAR are ectodysplasin receptors, which is one proposed reason the phenotype is restricted to skin appendages.

nodes.description: Each tumor inactivates the retained wild-type CYLD allele. Loss of heterozygosity of 16q is the commonest route (about two thirds of tumors with a detected second hit), and intragenic somatic mutation accounts for the rest; apart from 16q LOH, CYLD-mutant tumors carry few copy-number changes. The tumors are of hair-follicle lineage. Tumor mapping in two large families found tumors concentrated at sites of hormonally stimulated hair follicles, which the authors interpret as those follicles being particularly vulnerable to loss of heterozygosity; that is an inference from tumor distribution, not a measured mutation rate.

nodes.description: Expression profiling of CYLD-mutant tumors against perilesional skin shows overexpression of TRKB (NTRK2) and TRKC (NTRK3), with membranous staining, increased ERK phosphorylation and BCL2 in cylindromas. TRK knockdown or the TRK inhibitor lestaurtinib reduced growth of 3D primary tumor cultures, which is the preclinical basis for topical TRK inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: Dysregulated TRK signalling is a therapeutic target in CYLD defective tumours.
evidence.snippet: Gene expression profiling of CYLD mutant tumours showed dysregulated tropomyosin kinase (TRK) signalling, with overexpression of TRKB and TRKC in tumours when compared with perilesional skin.

evidence.reference_title: Dysregulated TRK signalling is a therapeutic target in CYLD defective tumours.
evidence.snippet: RNA interference-mediated silencing of TRKB and TRKC, as well as treatment with the small-molecule TRK inhibitor lestaurtinib, reduced colony formation and proliferation in 3D primary cell cultures established from CYLD mutant tumours.

nodes.description: Topical pan-TRK inhibitor tested in the TRAC trial (ISRCTN75715723). It was well tolerated, but in the randomized phase 2a part only 2 pegcantratinib-treated tumors met the response criterion against 6 placebo-treated tumors, so the prespecified efficacy endpoint was not met; the authors attribute this to low tumor drug concentrations. Not an established treatment.

evidence.snippet: 2 tumors treated with pegcantratinib achieved the primary outcome measure of response compared with 6 tumors treated with placebo. The primary prespecified number of responses was not met.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting Tropomyosin Receptor Kinase in Cutaneous CYLD Defective Tumors With Pegcantratinib: The TRAC Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.snippet: In this study, pegcantratinib, 0.5% (wt/wt), applied once daily appeared to be well tolerated and to penetrate the tumor tissue; however, the low tumor drug concentrations demonstrated are likely to account for the lack of response.

nodes.description: Topical salicylate was tried on the rationale that it blocks the NF-kappaB activation caused by CYLD loss. In a pilot of 12 target cylindromas in 5 patients, 2 showed complete remission and 8 a lesser response. It has not become standard care; a later paper describes a significant response in only a small proportion of treated tumors.
